neutral_facts.value: The accused were involved in a verbal altercation with the deceased, who had previously forbidden the accused from visiting his house and threatened to kill him if he did so again. During the altercation, the accused threw a stone at the deceased, which injured him, and the accused used a sword to inflict further injuries. The deceased succumbed to his injuries after being taken to the hospital. The prosecution relied on eyewitness accounts, medical evidence, and recovered weapons to establish the sequence of events leading to the deceased's death. The medical evidence indicated that the injuries were consistent with the use of a stone and a sword, and the witnesses confirmed the presence of both weapons at the scene.

quotes.text: The three witnesses namely PWs 8, 18 and 16 have clearly testified about the sequence of events leading to the death of the deceased which version has been found to be reliable by the courts below. There is no reason to strike a discordant note, for there is hardly any infirmity in the depositions of the above-mentioned witnesses, which have stood the test of lengthy cross-examination by the defence.

witness_credibility.value: The fact that the deceased suspected his wife's fidelity and an illicit intimacy with appellant No.1 is sufficiently proved from the deposition of the widow of the deceased (PW-16), and the other two witnesses (PWs 8 and 18). The presence of the two eye witnesses on the spot at the time of occurrence in a place like a bus stand is in no way abnormal to cast any doubt about their credibility.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that for a conviction under Section 302 IPC, there must be evidence of intention to cause death or shared intention to cause death. The court also relied on the principle that the prosecution must prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
